findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards state and the context, breaking log-call assertions
findings.body: TestLogger.FromContext always returns a brand-new TestLogger (`NewTestLogger()`), ignoring the input context and discarding any reference to the original TestLogger instance. Now that LoggerMiddleware calls `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` instead of `m.logger.Info(...)`, any test that passes a TestLogger into NewLoggerMiddleware and later asserts on that same TestLogger's InfoLogs/DebugLogs/etc. fields will never see the call recorded, because the actual Info() call happens on a disposable logger returned by FromContext. This silently makes such test assertions pass/fail incorrectly (false negatives), hiding real logging bugs rather than catching them.

findings.title: Logger interface extended with FromContext — breaking change for other implementers
findings.body: A new method FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger was added to the plugins/log.Logger interface. Any type implementing this interface outside of the two updated implementations (grafanaInfraLogWrapper and TestLogger) will fail to compile or satisfy the interface. This is an interface-breaking change that should be called out explicitly and verified against all implementers/consumers in the codebase (and potentially downstream plugin SDK usages) before merging.

findings.title: No unit tests for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware
findings.body: The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware (and its instrumentContext helper moved from the metrics middleware) has no dedicated test file added in this PR, even though it contains non-trivial logic for building contextual log attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) per RPC method. Since LoggerMiddleware now depends entirely on this middleware having run earlier in the chain to produce correct log output, lack of coverage for this middleware (e.g., verifying attributes added/omitted for datasource vs non-datasource contexts, or for user-less contexts) is a meaningful test gap.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware silently loses pluginId/endpoint/user/datasource log fields if middleware ordering changes
findings.body: logRequest no longer receives pluginCtx or endpoint; it now solely relies on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` picking up contextual attributes that were injected earlier in the chain by ContextualLoggerMiddleware (via log.WithContextualAttributes). This couples LoggerMiddleware's correctness to being registered strictly after ContextualLoggerMiddleware in CreateMiddlewares (pkg/services/pluginsintegration/pluginsintegration.go). There is no compile-time or runtime check enforcing this ordering — if the middleware list is ever reordered or ContextualLoggerMiddleware is removed/disabled, the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line will silently stop containing pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, and uname fields with no error or warning, degrading observability without any obvious failure signal.

findings.title: Test function name not updated after middleware rename
findings.body: The test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware even though the file was renamed to metrics_middleware_test.go and the type under test is now MetricsMiddleware. This is inconsistent with the stated purpose of the PR (renaming Instrumentation->Metrics for clarity) and will confuse future readers/searchers looking for tests of MetricsMiddleware.

findings.title: Stale logger name 'plugin.instrumentation' used for the renamed LoggerMiddleware
findings.body: NewLoggerMiddleware(cfg, log.New("plugin.instrumentation")) still uses the old 'instrumentation' terminology for the logger name, even though this PR's whole purpose is to rename Instrumentation to Metrics for clarity and this logger name is now used by LoggerMiddleware (not MetricsMiddleware). This leaves a misleading log channel name in log output that no longer corresponds to any component called 'instrumentation'.
